doc.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Writing the United Nations Earth Summit theme
summary: Levin tells how a documentary producer led to his writing an anthem with Pat Bianco, performed several times at the UN General Assembly.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. Well tell me about some of these — I don’t know if these things have any particular significance or not — but some of the compositions you’ve done, some of the jobs. The United Nations Earth Summit theme in ’92.

Yeah. It was. Over the years I’ve always thought being a musician, any musician that you talk with this way on camera or just hit them in a bar, if they could start telling stories you’ll have trouble getting out of the room. They’d go on forever. Any musician can do that. I’ve always thought that — first of all I’m lucky, very fortunate to be an active performing musician other than the fact that it’s something that I love and people actually pay me money to do it, which never ceases to amaze me, and the phone usually rings, which never ceases to amaze me. But I’ve always felt that musicians, especially because © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

they get to travel and you never work in the same place twice — well sometimes you do — but you work in so many different places. It’s not like you’re going to your office everyday. It’s always different. So you get into a lot of unique situations and there are a lot of unique opportunities. And you never know what’s going to happen when the phone rings. It could take you anywhere, to some country you’ve never been to before, to playing a style of music that you’ve never played before. Just all kinds of possibilities. That United Nations thing, I had underscored a documentary from somebody I met, a writer and producer and organizer, his name is Preni Gupti, he is Indian obviously. He’s been involved in the United Nations for years and was doing documentaries about India. And he is a good documentary filmmaker. And I don’t even remember how I met him, honestly. I think I was working for somebody else and then maybe I kind of met him, it’s that kind of interface thing happened. But I met him and I did a couple of low budget TV documentaries for him. And he came back to me one day and said he was involved with the Earth Summit coming up for the UN And he thought it’d be nice, we should have some music. So he said, “Pete, why don’t you write something?” I said well sure, okay. I didn’t know what it was going to come to. I wrote a kind of anthemy piece and I got a friend involved, a sax player-singer named Pat Bianco that I’ve done pop gigs with and even a few weddings. And he helped with the lyrics and we put this thing together, and went into the studio and recorded it. And it was passed around the UN And then Preni called back and said, “Listen there’s a big gathering in the General Assembly coming up, why don’t you come and perform it?” I says, “Wait a minute, you’re talking about THE General Summit? That one? The one with the —” Yeah it was — we did it actually three or four times. One of them they were dedicating a huge artwork that a Russian artist had just done. And so they opened the whole event with Pat and I sitting there, just piano and sax and vocal and we played it to a couple of thousand people, like dignitaries from all over the world, just sitting. Pat also shaves his head. A couple of bald guys sitting up there you know, just into it, doing what we do. Robert Rauschenberg I remember, he was sitting on the end of the dais there and he is known for taking a nip or two. And he was just kind of sitting there watching with this big grin on his face going like this. He was having a great time. And then Mario Cuomo got up and he started his speech by saying how great it was to come off the street where everything is hectic and just have some music to start with. It was great. I mean I never made a nickel from it, I think I would have been embarrassed if I did. And they went on to the big summit in Rio, which we were not involved in, but just the experience of playing in the General Assembly was pretty amazing.
